articles.title: Luka Doncic supera a Michael Jordan en la NBA: 308 vs 303
articles.summary: Luka Doncic suma 308 puntos en los primeros 8 partidos de la temporada 2026-2027 de la NBA. Michael Jordan sumó 303 puntos en los primeros 8 partidos de la 88-89.
articles.body: Luka Doncic suma 308 puntos en los primeros 8 partidos de la temporada 2026-2027 de la NBA. Michael Jordan sumó 303 puntos en los primeros 8 partidos de la 88-89. El ex del Real Madrid, que suma tres partidos seguidos anotando al menos 40 puntos, registró en el triunfo de los Lakers ante los Kings su sexto partido consecutivo con más de 35 puntos, 5 rebotes, 5 asistencias y 5 triples anotados (la racha más larga en la historia de la NBA) y se convierte en el primer jugador, desde Michael Jordan en la temporada 1988-89, en alcanzar más de 300 puntos en sus primeros ocho partidos de la temporada.

articles.title: Muere con 43 años Taurian Fontenette, el mito del streetball que ejecutó el primer mate de 720º
articles.standfirst: Taurian Fontenette es catalogado como "posiblemente el mejor especialista en mates que ha existido"
articles.summary: Taurian Fontenette es catalogado como "posiblemente el mejor especialista en mates que ha existido"
articles.body: Taurian Fontenette, mito del 'streetball' que popularizó AND1, ha muerto con 43 años. La leyenda del baloncesto callejero, que fue conocido como 'Air Up There' y 'Mr. 720', jugó profesionalmente en los Dallas Generals de la ABA. Su hermana confirmó la noticia y aún no se ha dado a conocer la causa de su muerte. La historia de Fontenette es sorprendente. Este escolta de 1,88 metros comenzó jugando para los Hitchcock Bulldogs y, posteriormente, pasó por diversas instituciones universitarias, como el Richland Junior College y el Paul Quinn College. Taurian trabajaba en seguridad en una planta química de Hitchcock cuando le pidió a su jefe un día libre para realizar una prueba con AND1; gracias a sus espectaculares mates, logró un puesto en el equipo del 'Mixtape Tour' en 2005. Un año después, hizo historia cerca de su casa: durante un partido de AND1 en el Toyota Center de Houston, realizó un mate de 720 grados —girando dos veces sobre su propio eje en el aire—, siendo esta la primera vez que se documentaba una acción de este tipo en un partido. Ahí nació el apodo de Mr. 720. Taurian Fontenette fue catalogado como "posiblemente el mejor especialista en mates que ha existido", y su movimiento más característico fue el Axle-Rider (un mate de 360 grados pasando el balón entre las piernas) que copiaron en la NBA jugadores como Jason Richardson, Paul George y Dennis Smith Jr.

articles.title: La noche de los monstruos
articles.standfirst: Wembanyama, Doncic, Shai y Jokic, aspirantes a MVP, muestran sus poderes en una macrojornada para la historia
articles.summary: Wembanyama, Doncic, Shai y Jokic, aspirantes a MVP, muestran sus poderes en una macrojornada para la historia
articles.body: En una macrojornada con 14 encuentros, los aspirantes al MVP de la NBA quisieron mostrar sus poderes al mismo tiempo. Victor Wembanyama, Luka Doncic, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander y Nikola Jokic, cuatro de los mejores jugadores del mundo se coordinaron para ofrecer exhibiciones que ya son parte de la historia de la competición. Fue la noche de los monstruos. Primero, la bestialidad de Wembanyama: en la victoria sobre los Mavericks (112-111) hizo 52 puntos y 24 rebotes, ambos topes en su carrera, además de poner ocho tapones. Esas cifras sólo las habían conseguido Bob McAdoo y el hombre récord Wilt Chamberlain. "Es que es básicamente Wilt Chamberlain", dijo su compañero Dylan Harper. Perfecta definición para lo que se vio. Al descanso, Wemby sumaba ya 29 puntos, 15 rebotes y cinco tapones, cifras nunca vistas en la historia de la NBA. Tres de los gorros llegaron en un intervalo de 13 segundos en el segundo cuarto cuando taponó sucesivamente a Cooper Flagg , PJ Washington y Daniel Gafford. Infranqueable. Lo peor para sus rivales es que actuaciones así pueden llegar a ser habituales. "Últimamente no me he sentido muy bien. Estoy enfermo. Sentí que recuperé la movilidad de las piernas. Así que debería ser así más a menudo", advirtió. La NBA tiembla. También con Doncic, que en su partido 100 con los Lakers hizo 40+9+7 en la victoria sobre los Kings (103-116) y lleva tres citas seguidas alcanzando la cuarentena y seis con 35. Con la camiseta la franquicia angelina, ese último registro sólo lo habían conseguido Kobe Bryant y Elgin Baylor. Ni ellos dos ni nadie añadió a sus actuaciones más de cinco rebotes, más de cinco asistencias y más de cinco triples anotados. Histórico. En los ocho primeros encuentros de esta temporada acumula ya 308 puntos, superando los 303 de Michael Jordan en la temporada 88-89. Así que el base esloveno se codea con los mitos mientras vive el que es "uno de los mejores momentos de mi carrera, pero aún queda trabajo por hacer". Sus compañeros alucinan. "Puedes llamarlo ola, puedes llamarlo tsunami, puedes llamarlo como quieras", afirmó Walker Kessler. Shai y Jokic no se quedaron atrás. El base de los Thunder se fue a los 42 puntos en el triunfo sobre los Cavaliers (124-116), a los que venía de meter 43 en el último encuentro. Así que 85 puntos y dos victorias ante el mismo rival en partidos consecutivos. Y el pívot de los Nuggets hizo 32 puntos, 10 rebotes y 11 asistencias para sumar su tercer triple-doble de la temporada y el 201 en su carrera. Ya está a ocho del récord de Russell Westbrook. El que logró ante los Raptors (128-109) fue el número 90 que logra en sólo tres cuartos. En el último, descansó. Y para rematar, LeBron James, que no estará en la carrera por el MVP pero a sus casi 42 años sigue ampliando sus récord. Hizo 13 puntos y con una de sus canastas alcanzó la colosal cifra de las 16.000 tiros de campo anotados en su carrera. Con la victoria sobre los Pistons (106-112), sus Sixers lideran la NBA con un balance de 8-1. "Demasiado pronto para hablar de las finales", advierte el mito, otro monstruo.

articles.title: 'You can fight Father Time': Klay Thompson's game-winning 3 seals Heat's comeback OT win over Clippers
articles.summary: After a slow start to the season, the longtime sharpshooter has begun to find his range, securing a sorely needed win for the Heat.
articles.body:
Through his first five games as a member of the Miami Heat, Klay Thompson was going through it. The longtime sharpshooter just couldn't find the range in his new home, missing more than two-thirds of his triple tries while struggling to keep up on defense for a Heat club that opened the season scuffling despite the offseason arrival of superstar Giannis Antetokounmpo.

On one hand, it seemed at least possible that Thompson — nearing his 37th birthday, coming off a pair of up-and-down campaigns in Dallas, years removed from his peak as a Splash Brother — just might no longer be the kind of flamethrowing gamebreaker we remember from his days with the dynastic Golden State Warriors. On the other, though … the guy who's made the fourth most 3-pointers in NBA history was going to get hot and swing a game at some point, right?

That point came at Intuit Dome, in Inglewood, Calif., with the visiting Heat trailing the Los Angeles Clippers by two points with 3.3 seconds remaining in overtime of a wild Wednesday night affair:

With the Heat inbounding from the frontcourt, Thompson begins the play by cutting from the free-throw line down toward the baseline, setting a pindown screen to allow Miami point guard Davion Mitchell to flash to the top of the key. That's just window dressing, though: When the Clippers switch that screen, Thompson turns and curls off a screen by Bam Adebayo.

The Heat big man picks off both L.A. defenders in the area, Kobe Sanders and Brook Lopez, giving Klay a clean release to the short corner. From Anthony Chiang of the Miami Herald :

"Bam set one heck of a screen," Spoelstra said. "Screeners don't usually get a lot of credit, but that's probably my best screen," Adebayo added with a smile.

"Bam set one heck of a screen," Spoelstra said.

"Screeners don't usually get a lot of credit, but that's probably my best screen," Adebayo added with a smile.

"I felt like I had so much space," Thompson said. "I'm not going to say that's an easy shot for me, but I've taken so many thousands of corner 3s, especially in that left corner. It's probably the easiest shot on the perimeter for a righty like myself. I got my feet down and planted, and it felt really good coming off my fingertips."

It looked even better splashing through the net, giving the Heat a one-point lead with one second remaining in OT. With no timeouts left, the Clippers could only attempt a three-quarter-court heave that came up empty, allowing Miami to escape with a 117-116 win .

Thompson's triple punctuated a remarkable comeback for the Heat. Miami had looked dead-to-rights in the first half, trailing by as many as 20 points and conceding a mammoth 30-4 run to their hosts fueled by the inside-out scoring of veteran center Lopez and rookie guard Keaton Wagler, who outscored the Heat in the second quarter 21-19 by themselves .

As they came out of intermission, though, the Heat began chipping away.

A defense that had given up 67 first-half points on 60% shooting tightened considerably, holding the Clips to 40 points on 35% shooting with eight turnovers across the third and fourth quarters. Antetokounmpo and Adebayo flexed their muscle, combining for 31 points and 17 free-throw attempts in the second half and the Heat whittled down L.A.'s lead; after a personal 6-0 run by Giannis, they were back within one possession just over a minute into the fourth quarter, putting the game back in the balance.

After a nip-and-tuck fourth quarter that saw the Clippers rebuild a double-digit deficit, the Heat promptly erased it to take a one-point lead on an Adebayo jumper with 1:53 remaining in regulation, and the Clips took back control on a layup by Darius Garland on the ensuing possession, both teams missed golden opportunities to put the game away. Perhaps the most damaging, though: A ghastly turnover by Garland near half-court — one of six on the night for the player who leads the league in cough-ups — that eventually allowed Antetokounmpo to step to the line for two free throws, putting Miami up by one with 10.8 seconds to go:

The Clips still had a chance to win it in regulation, though, with Rui Hachimura drawing a foul on a bang-bang play that was initially called a blocking foul on Pelle Larson. Miami challenged the call, arguing that it should've been a charge; officials deemed that challenge successful, but also called a proximate foul on Adebayo on the play after review, sending Hachimura to the line with 2.7 ticks remaining. He split his pair of free throws, though, and after a missed foul-line jumper by Adebayo on the other end, the game headed to overtime, knotted at 107.

L.A. charged back in front in overtime, with Garland scoring nine of his team-high 26 points in the extra frame. But a jumper by Adebayo got the Heat back within two heading into the final minute, and Thompson's literal last-second 3 stood up as the final margin — much to the relief of the always-intense Erik Spoelstra.

The game-winner was the eighth long-ball of the night for Thompson, who finished with 30 points on 11-for-22 shooting — his first 30-point game in two and a half years . Wednesday's performance continued a tear for the five-time All-Star and four-time NBA champion, who's gone 19-for-36 from long distance over the last three games as he thaws out from that frosty start.

"He's getting his legs under him, and he's getting his game legs," Spoelstra said of Thompson, according to Eric Nehm of The Athletic . "He's in shape, he works, he's really been putting in a lot of time. [...] You can fight Father Time and he's doing it. He's putting in a ton of time on his body, getting in shape, and that's allowing him to show the skill set that he's had throughout his Hall of Fame career."

Thompson, for his part, said after the win that he hasn't "felt this good in a long time."

"No pain in my lower limbs, and I'm so grateful to be here," he said, according to Chiang at the Herald . "I mean, they hold me accountable, the training staff and coaching staff, and I feel amazing. I haven't felt this good to start a season in years, so I'm just really inspired by not only my performance tonight, but our team's."

With the win, Miami improved to 3-5 heading into Thursday's date with Thompson's old friends in Golden State. The Clippers, on the other hand, have now lost seven in a row since winning on opening night, plunging to the bottom of the Western Conference standings alongside the Sacramento Kings and Utah Jazz.

articles.title: “There’s so much more I could learn about myself”: How LeBron James' wife Savannah found more than a business partner in her longtime friend April McDaniel
articles.summary: Some friendships become a part of a person's life in ways that go beyond everyday conversations.
articles.body: Some friendships become a part of a person's life in ways that go beyond everyday conversations. For Savannah James, wife of NBA superstar LeBron James, her bond with April McDaniel has grown into something much bigger over the years. The two women have supported each other through personal changes, difficult moments and new beginnings. Now, after nearly 17 years of friendship, they are also building businesses together.Their story did not begin with a business plan. It started with a meeting in Las Vegas and grew through years of honest conversations. April became someone Savannah could turn to, while Savannah offered the same support when her friend needed it.How Savannah James and April McDaniel helped each other through difficult timesSavannah and April first met at an NBA event in Las Vegas when Savannah was pregnant. April noticed her and made sure she was comfortable. Remembering that first meeting in a 2024 interview with PEOPLE, Savannah recalled April telling her, “Girl, what are you doing? Come over here and sit down.”That small moment was an early sign of the warmth that would become a part of their friendship. Over the years, they stayed close through different stages of life. Their conversations also became a space where they could speak honestly about things they were working through.April faced a particularly difficult period after losing her husband in 2013. She began focusing on her personal growth and started attending therapy. She often shared what she was learning with Savannah after her sessions.“Girl, guess what happened in therapy?” April recalled saying during a 2024 interview with Bustle.Those conversations also encouraged Savannah to look at her own life differently. Motherhood had become such a big part of her identity that she had not always given herself the same attention.“Before, I was just a mom. That’s where I felt my validity was. I put all my eggs in that basket without even trying to look outside of it. Once April and I started to have these conversations, I went, ‘Wow, there’s so much more I could learn about myself.’Their friendship has never been about agreeing with each other all the time. Savannah believes in being honest with April while also making sure she feels supported. In her PEOPLE interview, she described that balance through a particularly warm image, saying she would be there “rubbing your back” when April needed comfort.It is that mix of honesty and reassurance that has helped them grow together. They can challenge each other without making the other person feel alone. How their friendship became a business partnershipTheir shared experiences eventually inspired them to create something together. In April 2024, Savannah and April launched the podcast Everybody's Crazy. Savannah explained to CNBC Make It that she wanted to do something enjoyable with her friend.“I felt like this is something fun that I want to do with my friend,” she said.The podcast gives people an opportunity to call in and speak openly about their experiences. The two wanted the conversations to feel relaxed and different from the usual celebrity podcast format.They later expanded their work with Let It Break, a wellness collective inspired by their individual journeys towards personal growth. The idea was to create a space where women could focus on themselves instead of constantly putting their responsibilities first.Savannah explained to Boardroom in September 2026 that the venture came from the personal development journeys she and April were pursuing separately. Their other business, Crown + Conquer, is April's creative agency, which she founded around a decade ago.Now, all three ventures are coming together under Signed, a new holding company designed to give the businesses the support and leadership needed to grow. The company also has backing from MarcyPen Capital Partners, formed through the merger of Marcy Venture Partners and Pendulum Opportunities.Savannah has also been open about the responsibility that comes with accepting outside investment. Speaking to Boardroom, she said, “As Black women, we don't have the same grace. They're waiting for you to fail.”For Savannah and April, building a company together is another chapter in a friendship that has already seen them through personal changes and difficult conversations. Their businesses may have given them a new professional identity, but the trust behind the partnership was built long before they became business partners.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: NBA Rookie Rankings: Cameron Boozer, Yaxel Lendeborg lead early list of first-year phenoms
articles.summary: Here's our first look at this talented rookie class.
articles.body:
We're only a little over two weeks into the NBA regular season. It may seem a bit early to check in on this year's collection of rookies, but if we are being honest … this group of talent is that good.

To me, the early part of the season is all about curiosity. Teams don't have all of their "go-tos" in place, game plans are not quite as firm, rotations are expanded, and teams are figuring out which combinations and schemes work. Why not apply that to these young players trying to find their way?

What feels unique this year is that there is so much new talent being asked to contribute right away on so many different teams. Taking a glimpse this early in the season allows us to see what is working well and to understand the areas of opportunity. Then we can track where growth takes place, where consistency solidifies, and what happens when some of these scouting reports get updated.

I am always one to gently tap the patience button with young players. A slow start can still bring important reps that aid in development down the line. A quick rise can be met with resistance and stagnation.

The best thing you can do as a rookie is showcase a knack for something you bring to the table every single night. The more you do that, the more opportunity you will have to showcase the other things you can do.

Here are my top 10 rookies early in the season:

If you're wondering why the Grizzlies were the league's last undefeated team and matched their best start in franchise history, you can point to Boozer, who last week became the second-youngest player in NBA history to record a triple-double . The versatility of his game, mixed with what the Grizzlies have wanted to do offensively, has been a hand-in-glove fit.

Boozer can be used at both the 4 and the 5. At the 4, his ability to space and keep things flowing allows Memphis to run actions on both sides of the floor. If teams want to switch, Boozer has no issue going right to the post. His ability to win mismatches has been key: patience on his catch, an effort to get to his spot. If help comes, he can pass it out, which allows Memphis to attack tilted defenses. When moved to the 5, his ability to screen, roll, and quickly get to space opens things up. The short-roll passing speaks for itself, but pay attention to his timing and footwork when he screens.

His ability to mix in catch-and-shoot 3s has helped, too, as some of his finishing skills continue to develop. His drives have been aggressive — he's at his best when he delivers a blow with his shoulder — but he will have to balance that with gathering early and finishing over size and length. If these are the building blocks at the start, Boozer is putting himself in a great spot to be impactful all year long.

Many things have jumped out at me about Lendeborg's start, but it's the trust he's earned from Steve Kerr that stands out. After Sunday's game against the Clippers, Kerr said: "We scored 124 points and Yaxel is the main reason that we were high-powered." Lendeborg is attacking in transition, and he's involved in pick-and-roll as both a ball-handler and a screener. There is a trust in his ability to see the floor, but also to attack matchups. The Warriors are running their ever-present post splits through him for him to score . He's confidently taken the keys and gotten off to the races.

The blend offensively has been impressive. The drives have been there: he's unafraid to deliver physicality and get to his spot, showing patience, shiftiness and good footwork, and doing what it takes to turn the corner. The passing has been underrated: once he draws help, the ball is out on time and on target. The 3s have added to the overall package: he's the first rookie in NBA history to have multiple games with six or more made 3s in his first seven games. And these aren't just the catch-and-shoot variety, these are pull-ups over the defense. There's a confidence that tells me these reps will pay off down the line.

From summer league to the preseason to the regular season, ruthless aggression has been the name of the game for Dybantsa. There is a level of force that he plays with, including the way he drives. He will have to work on the balance between pull-ups and initiating contact on drives, but what we've seen is an ability to find a way to get to his spots. You feel him the most in the open court — it's almost as if he is gliding at times — and the result could be a pull-up, a spin, or a finish at the rim.

Being paired with Trae Young and Anthony Davis is a good launching point for Dybantsa, giving him plenty of runway without having to carry a large amount of playmaking responsibility. There have been flashes of what he can be as a playmaker, reading defenses and nailing skip passes. He can get to those types of plays within the flow of the offense off wide pindowns without having to create every single one. I am intrigued to see how he builds on his defensive potential, too. There's a level of physicality and activity he displays when his man is in off-ball actions. He needs that to translate to consistent screen navigation.

Wilson had at least 15 points, 1 steal and 1 block in his first six games, which is tied for the second-longest streak by a rookie to start a career. He plays with consistent and kinetic energy in transition whether he has the ball or not. That's the area where he's felt the most comfortable attacking for himself and his teammates. The mix of his shots will be key going forward: he's shooting 68.4% from the restricted area, but 33% or below in other shot areas. He's been a very willing 3-point shooter (44 of his 63 3PA have come from above the break), and when it's falling, it's dynamic.

He's at his best defensively when he's able to showcase his athleticism and timing. Running through passing lanes to get a steal. Appearing out of nowhere to get a block near the rim. He has a knack for being in help position off-ball and closing the window on a pass that seemed opened. Different matchups will produce different outcomes, but one thing that has not shifted is his will to compete.

It appears Acuff will be a lightning rod for those who enjoy the sport of discourse. My brain wonders whether that should take away from what he does well. How much do we factor in the context in Sacramento? How important is the production? And how do we track the improvement? One thing is for sure: He is an electric scorer. He's the first rookie since Luka Dončić in 2018-19 to have three straight games of 25 points, 5-plus rebounds and 5-plus assists. He's currently a top-10 scorer in the NBA. He also just so happens to be taking as many shots a night as Luka and Shai, and maybe that's where the eyebrows get raised.

Acuff is a tough shot-maker, which by default also makes him a tough shot-taker. The misses are going to feel loud. But is he taking what the defense gives him, or is he aggressively seeing space as an invitation to take a stepback or attempt to turn the corner? What's the balance between him making quick decisions and waiting to come off a screen? His scoring is drawing attention from defenses. The Pelicans worked to get to the level and put two on the ball (which opened up some passes). The Lakers not only put Matisse Thybulle on him but also gave him the switch-and-double treatment. Getting those types of reps early has value.

Flemings has grown during this early stretch of the season by taking reliable qualities (effort, defense, passing) and building on top of them. He plays with poise, composure, and certainty. He has a feel for the game and an understanding of where the ball needs to go and when. That's a great quality for a young guard, and even better for a young guard who has speed.

It rarely feels like he relies on the turbo button. He works to get in space, and works to engage bigs. He's not afraid to take a pull-up or turn the corner, but he's perfectly fine taking what the defense gives him and making the right play out of it. There have even been moments where he has seen a defensive coverage, let them recover, and then attacked the other way. That does not mean it's automatic every time down the court, but that ability, plus his lack of fear, is a positive sign going forward.

Despite the expectations and the early results in Utah, Peterson is doing a very important thing for a rookie: He's figuring it out. A Jazz offense based on flow, tempo and movement felt like one Peterson would immediately add to. The rhythm has been slightly off to start the season. There can be a bit of a learning curve to find the gaps in which to place your talent.

In spite of that, the best moments from Peterson have come when he's decisive. Win, lose or draw, a quick decision has allowed him to make the right reads and make the right plays. Adjusting to ball pressure and physicality has not changed his ability to read defenses. In fact, he's consistently worked to play at his speed, mixing in bursts but trying to have a constant cadence to his play in pick-and-roll. If and when the full array of shot-making returns to form (the 3 has been there), the overall package may feel even stronger.

Energy and effort can sometimes come across as buzzwords. But if you turn on a Denver Nuggets broadcast, you're going to see Brazile make a play. On either end of the floor. A block at the rim, a lob catch, an attack in transition. He's going to do something . He's brought a consistent level of effort to a Nuggets team that has needed it.

He has a knack for cutting from the corner or flashing around the dunker spot that fits right into what Denver wants to do (especially playing with Nikola Jokić). Defensively, his ability to rotate, close out, contain drives and contest has been a bright spot. To put it simply: he's all over the place (in a good way).

Mara's preseason showed once again that the Thunder would have a quality basketball player ready to contribute to their machine. The injuries that have been thrown at the Thunder mean Mara will have to contribute a little more quickly than expected.

Mara's defense has shown both his potential and where he can contribute right now. Having the ability to protect the rim with size is one thing; doing it in different ways is another. He has showcased the ability to rotate from the elbow or wing and be in position. Knowing how and when to execute different pick-and-roll schemes with the Thunder's defenders is another positive. His passing ability, meanwhile, fits right into a team that was working toward more movement and having multiple actions running on both sides. With his size and touch, rolling is a given, but being able to flash into open areas will help.

The biggest thing that has stood out to me from Brown is his moxie. No matter what the box score or scoreboard says, if you watch him, you cannot tell exactly how things are going. He has good speed and good skill, but the fun is watching when he truly understands how to use that speed: when to change speeds to throw a defender off and find an advantage, and when to attack in transition, off handoffs or in pick-and-roll.

The passing is something I have also enjoyed watching. He just zips the ball where it needs to go. The shot may bring him to the dance, but the ability to dip into making plays is where the balancing act becomes fun — the moments where he's unafraid to explore space in pick-and-roll and see if he can get to the second level of a defense, or get a defense to help. There's also a willingness on the defensive end that I think will serve him in the long run.

articles.title: Draymond Green Rips Dillon Brooks, Won't Respect His 'Energy' After Altercation in Warriors-Suns
articles.summary: Golden State Warriors star Draymond Green didn't buy Dillon Brooks' explanation after the Phoenix Suns wing said he wanted to "de-escalate" a tense situation in Monday's game between the two teams.
articles.body:
Golden State Warriors star Draymond Green didn't buy Dillon Brooks' explanation after the Phoenix Suns wing said he wanted to "de-escalate" a tense situation in Monday's game between the two teams.

"You weren't trying to de-escalate," Green said on his podcast. "You were trying to be the villain. But then don't go to the media like 'I was de-escalating.' Like, that's wack, and that type of energy will not ever be respected."

Green said he felt compelled to respond after Suns center Khaman Maluach knocked him to the court. The four-time All-Star grabbed Maluach around the waist and threw him down.

From there, Brooks intervened and created another flash point.

To Green's point, things appeared to be settling down quickly after he got his retribution. The moment was already de-escalating.

Even if he had the best intentions in mind, Brooks' reputation preceded him as well. The 30-year-old revels in his "villain" label and riling up opposing players. When he inserts himself into the picture, you're assuming he's not trying to play peacemaker.

The matter is pretty much closed for the time being. The NBA reportedly isn't suspending Green.

The next meeting between Golden State and Phoenix on Dec. 28 could have some extra spice, though.

articles.title: Paige Bueckers Wins 2026 WNBA Dawn Staley Community Leadership Award
articles.summary: Dallas Wings guard Paige Bueckers was named the WNBA's 2026 recipient of the Dawn Staley Community Leadership Award, the league announced on Thursday morning.
articles.body:
Dallas Wings guard Paige Bueckers was named the WNBA's 2026 recipient of the Dawn Staley Community Leadership Award, the league announced on Thursday morning.

Bueckers, who just played in her second WNBA season, has given back to the community going back to her college days as a star for UConn. The league's press release noted her efforts to combat food insecurity and support students in Minnesota through basketball and mentorship.

Additionally, Bueckers worked with Gatorade to refurbish a court in Minnesota and gave a $25,000 donation to nonprofit Athletic Committed Enlightened Scholars, and held a free basketball camp for nearly 100 middle and high school girls in Minnetonka, Minnesota. In Dallas, Bueckers worked in the Wings' annual Unified Game with Special Olympics of North Texas and participated in numerous other iniatives.

"Paige Bueckers embodies the spirit of what this award, established in my name, represents," said Dawn Staley in a statement. "Through her leadership, compassion, and commitment to service, Paige uses her platform to uplift communities and inspire the next generation. I'm proud to honor her for making a difference that reaches far beyond basketball."

The award honors WNBA Hall of Famer and current South Carolina head coach Dawn Staley and recognizes a current WNBA player who "reflects Staley's spirit, leadership, charitable efforts, love for the game, and inspirational presence." It has been a league postseason award since 2008.

"With every partnership I take on, it's really important to me to include a charity or community engagement component," Bueckers said in a statement. "I've been fortunate to have so many people and communities invest in me throughout my life, and I want to pay that forward by using my platform to create opportunities for the next generation. Whether that's through sports, education, food security or mentorship, I want to make sure people have access to opportunities they might not otherwise have. Sports have given me so much, and I think they can be such a powerful way to bring people together, build community and create opportunity."

articles.title: Klay Thompson Explains Why He 'Feels Young Again' After Joining Heat, Says He's 'Locked In' on Diet
articles.summary: Miami Heat guard Klay Thompson is loving his time in town after signing a two-year contract with the team last summer, and he explained why in an exclusive interview with Mark Medina for Fadeaway World, which dropped Thursday, noting that the organization makes him "feel young again."
articles.body:
Miami Heat guard Klay Thompson is loving his time in town after signing a two-year contract with the team last summer, and he explained why in an exclusive interview with Mark Medina for Fadeaway World, which dropped Thursday, noting that the organization makes him "feel young again."

"It's been a tough start to the season," Thompson began. "But I feel like I'm enjoying my time very much. The competitiveness in this organization is second to none. I feel incredible. I feel young again for how hard they train me. I'm inspired that I have great seasons ahead. That's what Miami has done so far. It really has reinvigorated my spirit for the game."

Thompson also said the team is really focusing on his physical health.

"A lot of running and making me accountable for my weight and body-fat percentage. I've locked in on my diet. It's all of those little things that you don't see that allow you to be your best athlete. I really love it. I feel like young again and motivated to be great again."

Thompson (and the Heat) endured a difficult beginning to 2026-27. The 36-year-old averaged just 7.8 points on 31.7 percent shooting over his first five contests. Miami lost its first four games.

However, Thompson has caught fire, averaging 24.7 points on 57.4 percent shooting while hitting 19-of-36 three-point attempts. Miami is now in a groove (three wins in its last four games).

On Wednesday, Thompson knocked down a game-winning three-pointer with one second left in overtime to lead his team to a 117-116 road win over the Los Angeles Clippers.

Thompson scored a season-high 30 points, making 8-of-17 threes in his 35 minutes.

The 14-season NBA veteran and five-time All-Star once enjoyed amazing success on the Golden State Warriors, helping his team win four NBA championships and six Western Conference titles.

He has also made an impressive return to action after missing two-plus seasons with a torn ACL (2019-20) and then a torn Achilles (2020-21 and part of 2021-22). Thompson notably helped the Warriors win the 2021-22 championship, averaging 19.0 PPG in the playoffs.

Thompson had a tough season last year with the Dallas Mavericks, posting career-lows in points (11.7 PPG) and field goal percentage (39.3 percent).

However, he's enjoyed a resurgence of late, and it's helped Miami turn its season around after a tough start. It's clear he loves the organization and what it's doing for his career, and that could foreshadow a strong comeback campaign.

articles.title: Lakers' Bronny James, Cameron Carr Assigned to G League Roster Ahead of Coachella Valley's Opener

articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers announced Thursday that guards Bronny James and Cameron Carr have been assigned to the the Coachella Valley Lakers, the team's G League affiliate.

Coachella Valley will open its season on Friday in Palm Desert.

James, 22, has appeared in 74 career games across three seasons with the Lakers—including five this season—while averaging 2.5 points and one assist in 7.7 minutes per game.

Carr, 21, was the No. 24 overall pick in the 2026 NBA draft and has barely seen the court, appearing in just three games while registering no stats.

Neither player was likely to see many minutes at the NBA level this season, barring injuries. The Lakers are stacked at guard, with Luka Dončić and Austin Reaves operating as the starters, Collin Sexton and Quentin Grimes the main reserves behind them and Jaden Hardy available as further depth.

At the 3, the Lakers have primarily utilized players like Matisse Thybulle and Ziaire Williams. With a fairly defined rotation early in the season, finding minutes outside of garbage time for James or Carr hasn't been terribly feasible or necessary.

articles.title: Saint Louis forward Robbie Avila granted injunction for fifth season of college basketball
articles.summary: Avila should be on the floor when St. Louis plays Missouri on Friday.
articles.body:
Saint Louis forward Robbie Avila is getting another season of college basketball.

Avila was granted a preliminary injunction Thursday by St. Louis City Circuit Court Judge Jason Sengheiser that allows him to play for the Billikens this season. As part of the injunction, Sengheiser says that SLU can have a 16th roster spot for Avila and that the order is effective until a trial is held.

Any trial wouldn't likely be held for months, meaning Avila could be eligible for the entirety of the 2026-27 season and will be in uniform on Friday night when Saint Louis plays Missouri.

Like many players from the high school class of 2022 across the country, Avila took to court for a fifth season of eligibility after exhausting four seasons of eligibility ahead of the NCAA's five-in-five announcement this summer. After his college career was seemingly over this spring when the Billikens were eliminated from the NCAA tournament, Avila played for the Los Angeles Lakers' summer league team but did not sign a contract with the franchise.

That scenario is not uncommon among basketball players who have asked for and received a fifth year of eligibility. Missouri's Mark Mitchell, who will be on the court Friday night as well, played for the Denver Nuggets' summer league team.

This will be Avila's third season with the Billikens after transferring to SLU when Josh Schertz, his coach at Indiana State, became the team's head coach. After averaging 17.3 points as a junior, Avila averaged 12.8 points per game in 2025-26 while also playing eight minutes fewer per game. He shot 41% from behind the arc on nearly five attempts per game and was the 2025-26 Atlantic-10 Player of the Year.

SLU went 29-6 a season ago and won the A-10 regular season title. That season was good enough for a No. 9 seed in the NCAA tournament, where the Billikens lost in the second round to eventual national champion Michigan.

articles.title: El Fenerbahce, sin piedad de un Baskonia sin alma
articles.standfirst: Kenneth Fared fue el mejor de los vitorianos y acabó con mnolestias
articles.summary: Kenneth Fared fue el mejor de los vitorianos y acabó con mnolestias
articles.body: El Fenerbahce no tuvo piedad este jueves y superó con comodidad a un mermado Kosner Baskonia, 84-65, que solo aguantó cinco minutos ante un equipo candidato a todo que se mantuvo invicto en casa en la décima jornada de la Euroliga. Los problemas en la pintura y en el tiro exterior -16 % de acierto- de los vitorianos comenzaron marcar diferencias con el equipo turco que mejoró por momentos y castigó a un equipo que se deshizo con el paso de los minutos. Kenneth Faried fue la única nota positiva de los visitantes, pero el pívot se retiró con molestias en el último cuarto. Talen Horton Tucker y Will Clyburn fueron los máximos anotadores del Fenerbahce, que tuvo una aportación muy coral y dejó sentenciado el choque al descanso. El único pívot nato azulgrana aguantó al Baskonia en el inicio de un partido anotador, en el que el triple local marcó el ritmo en el marcador. Con la rotación, el equipo de Velimir Perasovic perdió altura y presencia física por las lesiones de sus interiores, pero buscó la velocidad para suplir esas carencias, mientras Dwight Powell, que debutaba en Europa de la mano de Sarunas Jasikevicius, era clave en el rebote ofensivo. Los turcos sumaban prácticamente en cada ataque, en varias ocasiones lo hacían de tres en tres y mandaron en el primer asalto por 33-18, donde la defensa y la concentración del equipo vasco fue clave. El uno contra uno de los manejadores del conjunto otomano marcaba diferencias, sobre todo cuando no estaba Faried. Los errores azulgranas se sucedían y la distancia creció por encima de los 20 puntos. El Baskonia sudaba cada punto en el cinco contra cinco y solo lograba sacar rendimiento con el contraataque, pero costaba bajar la diferencia ante un equipo que dominó 52-32 en una primera mitad en la que la aportación de Kenneth Faried no era suficiente. Braxton Key hacía daño en la agrietada pintura del Baskonia, que no encontraba la forma de meterle mano a la maquinaria turca. El desacierto desde el triple era un lastre para los azulgranas que ni siquiera podían sumar desde el tiro libre. Horton-Tucker comenzó a entrar en el partido y los focos ofensivos del equipos de Sarunas Jasikevicius se multiplicaron hasta el 63-41, tras un periodo muy igualado. Los azulgranas llegaron a firmar un acierto de tres puntos de 18 intentos, lo que marcó la tendencia de un partido en el que fue expulsado a Wade Baldwin en el comienzo del último acto. El Baskonia intentó maquillar en la recta final un partido roto que acabó con un 84-65. 84 - Fenerbahçe (33+19+11+21): Larkin (6), Forrest (1), Shields (9), Key (13) y Bingham (9) -cinco inicial-, Baldwin IV (8), Melli (3), Horton-Tucker (19), Juzang (3), Powell (3), Clyburn (10) y Sargiunas (-). 65 - Baskonia (18+14+9+24): Lawson (5), Simmons (12), Joksimovic (7), Frisch (10) y Faried (10) -cinco inicial-, Stewart (12), Duarte (-), Spagnolo (3) y Baugh (6). Árbitros: Sasa Pukl (Eslovenia), Milos Koljensic (Montenegro) y Joseph Bissang (Francia). Sin eliminados. Expulsaron a Baldwin con dos técnicas (min. 32) y señalaron falta técnica a Key (min. 39). articles.title: Kevin Durant Says 'It's All Love' at Rockets Presser After Trending Video of Exchange With Reporter
articles.summary: Houston Rockets star Kevin Durant tried to set a different tone inside the media room after an earlier back-and-forth with the Houston Chronicle's Varun Shankar made the rounds on social media.
articles.body:
Houston Rockets star Kevin Durant tried to set a different tone inside the media room after an earlier back-and-forth with the Houston Chronicle 's Varun Shankar made the rounds on social media.

Following Wednesday's 117-107 loss to the Minnesota Timberwolves, Durant opened his press conference by saying it's "all love" and a "family atmosphere in here."

"We go back and forth. We can do that," he said. "Can we not? Make your minions online know that too. I got attacked; you got popular the last couple of days."

LeBron's KD and Steph Scouting Reports 📋

The vibes were a little different Monday night, when Shankar brought up Durant's relatively low shot count in a 109-93 win over the Boston Celtics. The 16-time All-Star took exception to the question given his team was victorious:

Whether he likes it or not, KD's usage is a subplot to the Rockets' start so far. His 12.4 field-goal attempts per game are the lowest of his career, and he hasn't averaged so few points (20.8) since his rookie season.

On its own, pointing those two facts out isn't a critique when Houston is second in offensive rating (120.0), per NBA.com . When he turned 38 in September and is into his 19th season, it makes sense for Durant to take more of a back seat, and the strategy is working.

Not all great players can successfully make the transition. Durant's ability to pull it off is further evidence of his status as a generational scorer.

Isolating a one-game sample can be deceptive, and nine games isn't statistically significant within the context of an entire season. Still, Durant's shot attempts is something worth talking about if the trend persists.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham dishes out some brutal honesty for her WNBA peers & coach high school football for $180K!
articles.summary: Sophie Cunningham calls out the WNBA's missed layups, Curt Cignetti takes aim at SEC bias, and the Dothan Wolves seek a $180K football coach.
articles.body: 'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday-Friday on OutKick.com. Over the hump and, somehow, safely onto the other side of the week. Whew. We made it. Barely. The stocks are rocky. The temperature in this country has been cranked WAY up. We're all just treading water right now. But hey, we're doing it together. We're in this for the long haul, folks. Stay the course. We've got Thursday Night Football tonight, and then we'll be off to the races. Big weekend of college football on tap. Big weekend of NFL. Thanksgiving, believe it or not, is three weeks from today. Right now. Right this second. Strap in. Hold on tight. Let's ride. Welcome to a Thursday Nightcaps — the one where Sophie Cunningham asks her WNBA peers the same question we've asked all season long ... Why can't y'all make a layup? Sophie's words, not mine! What else? I've got Curt Cignetti back on the campaign trail even though the election is over, Luka Doncic berating a fan for a perfectly executed chest pass, and if you're looking to make some quick holiday money, there's a job opening for a high school football coach in Alabama that you might wanna take a look at. Lordy. It just means more, baby! OK, grab you a donut for National Donut Day, and settle in for a Thursday 'Cap! Sophie Cunningham isn't blind I've got no real hot take on donuts. Who doesn't like a donut? Boston cream is obviously the GOAT, followed by blueberry and then just a simple glazed. Short, simple and easy. When it comes to donuts, I think you have to go simple. We go on vacation every year to a spot down here in Florida that I won't name because it's already too crowded as it is, and they have one of those fancy donut shops by the beach. They have every topping known to man at their disposal, and folks go NUTS with their custom creations. Fruity Pebbles on top. Reese's Pieces. Key lime pie frosting. Sriracha! Hogwash. Give me a simple donut done correctly, and it'll beat anything Gen-Z decides to create. I promise. And that concludes the culinary portion of today's class. You're welcome! Now, let's get this show on the road with Sophie Cunningham wondering why nobody in the WNBA can make a layup. Frankly, it's a fair question. Curt Cignetti is back to stirring the pot "Why do we miss so many wide open layups? It's a joke. What the f--k is that?" She's right, by the way. I'm just glad someone finally asked. Obviously, I never watched a single WNBA game until Caitlin Clark came into the league. Nobody did. But, I've had to dabble in the league for content purposes over the past few years, and I've gotta tell you ... I was STUNNED when I watched my first WNBA game. Stunned. ANGEL REESE SETS TWO WNBA RECORDS WITH HISTORIC REBOUNDING PERFORMANCE The amount of missed shots around the basket is jarring. Angel Reese does this all the time. In fact, she does it so much, society made up the term "mebound" for her because she pads her stats by grabbing so many of her missed shots. I also like how Sophie immediately pushes back on her partner's long line of excuses (athleticism, strength, height, etc ...): "Dude these are, like, wide open layups." Amazing. She's the best. OK, let's keep this class moving and check in on Curt Cignetti in the wake of Tuesday's first batch of College Football Playoff rankings. He seems pleased! Luka, 'Bama & the Big Ten "SEC gets a lot of love from ESPN, you know, and all their writers that they don’t technically pay, but march to their drum. So, and that’s why you see all these SEC teams up there, you know, and some good two-loss teams from the Big Ten, not quite as high. But like I said, it’s all going to be it’s all going to be played out on the field." Whoaaaaaaaaaa Nellie! Tell us how you really feel, Curt! Who, exactly, are the good two-loss teams from the Big Ten? I'm genuinely curious, because this is a down year for the Big Ten. A DOWN year. Michigan stinks. Penn State stinks. Oregon has no QB, and stinks. USC looks better because they just beat Ohio State, but let's be real about that one for a second. The Trojans lose that game by two touchdowns if Ohio State has a competent person throwing the ball. So who is it? Iowa? Come on. Maybe Northwestern. I can make a case for Northwestern because that program has been solid, even though they lost a game they should've won last week against Oregon. But other than that? I'm just not seeing it. The committee may very well have an SEC bias — I don't think Alabama deserves to be No. 5, and I wrote that yesterday — but using two-loss Big Ten schools as the argument ain't it. Not this year, at least. OK, let's rapid-fire this Thursday class into a big Thursday night. First up? Speaking of Alabama, let's check in on the local high school football scene as the postseason gets underway: That's real, by the way. This is from the school's official Facebook post: Dothan City Schools is seeking a Head Football Coach to lead the Dothan High School Wolves football program! Annual Salary: $150,000–$180,000 The ideal candidate will: • Build a championship-caliber program with a vision for sustained success and state title contention. • Lead and develop a high-performing coaching staff committed to excellence and accountability. • Demonstrate a proven record of success in varsity competition, playoff appearances, and championship-level performance. • Prioritize student-athlete growth through academic achievement, character, discipline, and well-being. • Establish a year-round culture of excellence through strategic preparation, teamwork, and community engagement. Any takers? Think you got what it takes to lead the Dothan Wolves to a championship? Let's see it! Hell, I'll throw my hat in the ring for $180,000. The cost of living in Dothan, for those wondering, is about 15% lower than the US average, according to Payscale.com. The medium home listing sits around $316,000. And hey! Look at this bad boy that's been on the market for 48 days now: And it's only a 20-minute drive to Dothan High! You're just not getting a better deal than that right now in America. Go get 'em, folks. You're welcome. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! OK, that's it for today. Good Thursday, everyone. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP On the way out, here's Lakers star Luka Doncic berating a fan — and eventually getting him ejected — because he deemed this toss to the ref a little too aggressive. Looks like a textbook pass to me. Soft! See you tomorrow.

articles.title: Tyrese Maxey Addresses 76ers' Ego Concerns, LeBron's Impact Amid Hot Start, 'Competitive as Hell'
articles.summary: The Philadelphia 76ers have begun the LeBron James era 8-1 and atop the NBA standings, and the vibes seem to be good despite early concerns about having too many big egos on the roster.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia 76ers have begun the LeBron James era 8-1 and atop the NBA standings, and the vibes seem to be good despite early concerns about having too many big egos on the roster.

NBC Sports Philadelphia reporter John Clark posted a video from the 76ers locker room on Thursday, where point guard Tyrese Maxey addressed some of that.

"We are competitive as hell. I see us playing hard, playing hard defensively, and playing together," he said. "That's who we are. That's not fluff. I found that out day one of training camp. We were moving the ball. All of the ego stuff and one ball stuff, LeBron is here and he has made everyone willing passers. When LeBron can be a willing passer, the rest of us can too."

The last four times James has been on a team that started the season at least 7-1, it has gone on to the NBA Finals.

The Sixers are coming off of a 112-106 win against Detroit on Wednesday night where James scored 13 points with 10 rebounds and eight assists. Maxey, who appeared to injure his right pinkie finger late in the game, is averaging 28.0 points per game and shooting 48.6% from the field.

articles.summary: El escolta lidera la cuarta victoria seguida de los azulgranas: comanda un parcial de 6-29 en el tercer cuarto y mete la canasta de la tranquilidad para acabar con 22 puntos
articles.body: Un Barça muy serio sigue creciendo en la Euroliga. Cuarta victoria consecutiva y en cancha de un candidato a playoffs como es el Hapoel Tel Aviv (90-93). A domicilio, balance de 4-1 para los azulgranas, que resistieron en los momentos más crudos y dieron un golpe determinante aprovechando un trance de Darío Brizuela. Cuando ‘La mamba vasca’ pica es realmente venenosa. Andaba el Barça algo tocado en el tercer cuarto, 60-53 tras haber estado nueve puntos abajo sufriendo un mal criterio arbitral y una lluvia de tiros libres cuando Brizuela entró en ignición. En un abrir y cerrar de ojos, 10 puntos seguidos con dos triples y una asistencia para otro de Stanley Umude. También con una gran defensa, creció el parcial hasta el 0-16 y, ya en el último periodo, a 6-29 para lo que parecía encarrilar la victoria (64-78). Mantuvieron los azulgranas una buena renta. A falta de 1:33 ganaban por nueve con un mate tras rebote ofensivo de Tosan Evbuomwan. Con 39 segundos por jugarse, Justin Robinson, que siempre aparece en el tramo final, anotó una bandeja para el poner un 85-91 que parecía definitivo. Error. Un triple de Vasilije Micic y un posterior robo con tiros libres de Elijah Bryant apretaron hasta el 90-91. Tuvo que ser Brizuela el que sentenciara a falta de cinco segundos con otra penetración para llegar a los 22 puntos. Micic falló desde lejos para forzar la prórroga. El Barça volvió a mostrar su capacidad para sobrevivir. Negado de inicio en el tiro (0/8 en triples), se agarró a los rebotes de ataque (16), un salvavidas durante toda la noche con un Josh Nebo enorme (12+10, seis de ellos ofensivos). Micic (24) encontraba una autopista al aro y el Hapoel mandaba: 16-6. Empezaron a entrar los triples y el Barça, de la mano de Robinson (20), dio la vuelta al marcador. Dan Oturu (11+7) ayudaba en un parcial de 9-0. Entre los tres pilares del Hapoel, 84 de los 98 de valoración. articles.title: Saint Louis Forward Robbie Avila, the A-10 Player of the Year, Gets Injunction to Play This Season
articles.summary: Saint Louis forward Robbie Avila, the Atlantic 10 player of the year who became a sensation for his signature specs at Indiana State, was granted a preliminary injunction Thursday to play a fifth season of college basketball for the Billikens.
articles.body:
Saint Louis forward Robbie Avila, the Atlantic 10 player of the year who became a sensation for his signature specs at Indiana State, was granted a preliminary injunction Thursday to play a fifth season of college basketball for the Billikens .

St. Louis City Circuit Court Judge Jason Sengheiser also ruled that Saint Louis can have a 16th roster spot for Avila until a trial is held, which could be several months from now, effectively clearing the 23-year-old to play for the entire season.

The ruling comes as the Billikens are preparing for a high-profile game against Missouri on Friday night.

Avila spent two seasons playing for Josh Schertz at Indiana State before following him to Saint Louis, where he averaged 17.3 points as a junior and 12.8 points last season. Overall, the 6-foot-10 forward has started 132 of his 137 career games.

Saint Louis has high hopes this season after going 29-6 and winning the A-10 regular-season title last season. The Billikens were a No. 9 seed for the NCAA Tournament, where they beat Georgia in the first round before losing to eventual champion Michigan.

Avila is the latest college athlete to win eligibility after the NCAA announced earlier this year that it was shifting to a "five-for-five" model, giving athletes five seasons to play over a five-year period, beginning when they turn 19 or graduate from high school, whichever is earlier. The rule was not intended to apply to those from the 2022 class who had exhausted their eligibility, touching off a wave of lawsuits filed by athletes in a variety of sports all over the country.

In most cases, judges have ruled in favor of the plaintiffs, many joined in their lawsuits by athletes similarly in limbo. But there is fear among players and coaches that appeals by the NCAA could ultimately go against them, rendering them ineligible again.

"The NCAA screwed up on this deal," Gonzaga coach Mark Few said recently. "You've got to be fair and let these (class of) 22's in."

Making the situation even more bizarre is that some of those athletes, including Avila, spent time playing for professional teams. In his case, Avila played for the Los Angeles Lakers during the NBA's summer league, though he never signed a pro contract.

Missouri forward Mark Mitchell, who will be facing Avila and the Billikens on Friday night, played for the Denver Nuggets over the summer. He was part of a lawsuit filed in Kentucky that won — for now — eligibility for 38 football and basketball players.

"I think these cases are going to go well into the season," Duke coach Jon Scheyer said recently. "I think no question you're going to have cases where certain players get an injunction, they're eligible for a certain period, and then they're not."

articles.title: El Valencia despierta a tiempo para igualar su mejor arranque en la Euroliga
articles.standfirst: Logró ante el Armani MIlán su séptima victoria en 10 partidos
articles.summary: Logró ante el Armani MIlán su séptima victoria en 10 partidos
articles.body: Armori Brooks jugó dos temporadas en Milán (sus dos primeras en Europa), por eso resulta más curioso que fuera él el que sellara el triunfo del Valencia, 73-84, ante el Armani en el Unipol Forum. Lo pasó mal el Valencia, le tocó remar cuando enfilaba el último cuarto por debajo en el marcador, 59-51, tras un horrible tercer cuarto (22-11). Pero en el tramo final apareció Brooks, un tirador excelso y, sobre todo la versión imparable de TJ Shorts que se adueñó del partido, para asegurar el séptimo triunfo del Valencia Basket en 10 partidos, igualando su mejor arranque histórico en la Euroliga. Una canasta de Corbalán a 3:21 para el final del partido dio el mando al Valencia (67-69) y ya no lo volvió a perder. De ahí al final los taronja ganaron ese minipartido de poco más de tres minutos con un 6-15, jugando mucho mejor el tramo decisivo. El Armani, con una canasta de Cole, puso el 73-75 a 1:38 pero 20 segundos después, Brooks abrochó el triunfo del Valencia con una prodigioso triple. El Valencia, que se medía contra uno de los dos equipos que tan sólo han ganado un partido en la Euroliga, arrancó como un cohete y en cinco minutos tenía casi el partido en la mano con un impresionante 2-20 de arranque. En ese momento lucían un 4/5 en triples y habían desarbolado por completo la frágil confianza italiana. Pero fue salir Leandro Bolmaro y cambiar el partido por completo. Al final del cuarto el Milán mostraba constantes vitales, 15-24, al llegar al descanso se habían metido en la pelea: 37-40 con el argentino y Ricci como protagonistas. El Valencia, que había metido cuatros de sus primeros cinco triples, se apagó para fallar 10 tiros seguidos desde el arco. había anotado 24 puntos en el primer cuarto y tan sólo 27 entre el segundo y el tercer periodo, complicándose y mucho la vida. La defensa del Armani había desactivado el ataque del Valencia (97,1 puntos de media hasta este choque). Pero Brooks y, sobre todo Shorts, aparecieron en el momento justo. El base, muy bien defendido y al que sacudieron de lo lindo, se rehizo para aparecer al final y llevar en volandas al Valencia. Taylor fue el mejor anotador taronja con 17, Brooks acabó con 16 con 4/9 en triples y Sako, en un gran partido en la pintura, acabó con 14. En el Armani, Bolmaro acabó con 16, Diop hizo 11 y Ricci, con 3/5 en triples, firmó 10.

articles.title: Bronny James assigned to G League's Coachella Valley Lakers after playing limited minutes early in third NBA season
articles.summary: James, who has averaged a mere 2.4 minutes in five appearances for the Lakers amid their 7-2 start, will join the G League affiliate ahead of its season open...
articles.body:
Bronny James made the Los Angeles Lakers' 2026-27 opening night roster, securing a spot while his draft classmate, first-round pick Dalton Knecht, was waived.

But after James averaged 2.4 minutes in five appearances amid the Lakers' 7-2 start, the team announced Thursday that it assigned the 2024 second-round pick to the G League's Coachella Valley Lakers.

Fellow guard Cameron Carr was also sent to the franchise's G League affiliate ahead of its Friday night season opener against the Utah Jazz's Salt Lake City Stars.

Bronny James — in his first season in the Lakers' organization without his father, LeBron James — previously spent time in the G League, where his stat lines have often dwarfed those he has authored in the NBA.

Across a combined 25 regular-season games the past two seasons with the then-South Bay Lakers — who have since relocated and rebranded — Bronny James posted 18.4 points, 4.4 assists, 4 rebounds and 1.5 steals per game while shooting 49.6% from the field, including 41.3% from beyond the arc.

James, now 22, was the No. 55 pick when he was drafted out of USC more than two years ago. He appeared in 27 regular-season games with the Lakers as a rookie, making father-son history but struggling mightily at times, particularly early on.

He made noticeable progress in Year 2, taking the court for 42 regular-season games and raising his field-goal percentage from 31.3% (2024-25) to 40.9% (2025-26) and his 3-point percentage from 28.1% (2024-25) to 38.6% (2025-26).

Head coach JJ Redick saw enough from James to include him in his playoff rotation last season, albeit a shorthanded one.

That paved the way for additional excitement and milestones .

Coming into Year 3, the question was: How would James fare without his superstar father on the Lakers ( including how would he be treated by staff and teammates in the absence of the future Hall of Famer )?

But James hasn't been given much of an opportunity in the regular season to make any kind of jump. In his sparing minutes, he scored 0.8 points per game. He attempted only three field goals and made two of them.

James could wind up back with the Lakers soon, but his lack of on-court involvement so far isn't promising, in terms of his chances of carving out the long-term 3-and-D role he teased on occasion last season.

As for Knecht, he ended up signing a two-way deal with the New York Knicks , for whom he logged 10 points on 4-of-6 shooting, plus seven rebounds, on Wednesday in a win over the Chicago Bulls.

articles.title: Los Lakers degradan a Bronny James
articles.standfirst: El base jugará en el equipo afiliado en la G League después de haber disputado sólo 12 minutos en lo que va de temporada NBA
articles.summary: El base jugará en el equipo afiliado en la G League después de haber disputado sólo 12 minutos en lo que va de temporada NBA
articles.body: Bronny James ha sido enviado al equipo vinculado en la G League, los Coachella Valley Lakers. El base de 22 años y 1,88 metros apenas había sido utilizado por el entrenador JJ Redick y la franquicia ha decidido que cambie de competición en busca de minutos para que pueda seguir desarrollando su juego. En lo que va de temporada, Bronny había aparecido en cinco partidos de los Lakers estando en pista un total de 12:23 minutos. En ese tiempo, sus cifras habían sido muy pobres: cuatro puntos y ningún rebote o asistencias. El peor dato, el +/-, que indica el resultado de un equipo mientras un jugador está en pista. Con él, pese a poco tiempo que ha jugado, los angelinos han perdido por 27. Recientemente, Bronny y el resto de suplentes de los Lakers fue criticado por Redick al perder en un minuto una amplia ventaja ante los Raptors cuando el partido estaba ya sentenciado. "No cometeré ese error de nuevo. Dejaré a los chicos en la cancha. Hay que jugar hasta el último segundo y si los suplentes no están listos para jugar, entonces simplemente no los pondré", dijo el técnico. Bronny ya había sido enviado a la G League en las dos temporadas anteriores, en las que coincidió en los Lakers con su padre. La competición parece encajar mejor con sus condiciones, pues ahí sí que ha tenido buenas actuaciones. En los 25 encuentros que ha disputado a lo largo de esos dos cursos, el base ha promediado 18,4 puntos con un 49,6% de acierto en tiros de campo, 4,4 asistencias y 4,0 rebotes. Junto a la opción de enviar a James a la G League, los Lakers estaban estudiando incluirle en algún movimiento que les permitiera reforzarse. De momento, sólo le han degradado.

articles.title: Kon Knueppel to miss Friday’s Hornets-Celtics clash with ongoing hamstring injury
articles.summary: On Wednesday evening, the Charlotte Hornets continued their ugly start to the season with a tough road loss at the hands of the Brooklyn Nets. Things went fr...
articles.body:
On Wednesday evening, the Charlotte Hornets continued their ugly start to the season with a tough road loss at the hands of the Brooklyn Nets. Things went from bad to worse in this one when shooting guard Kon Knueppel exited the lineup with an apparent hamstring injury.

This game marked Knueppel's first contest of the season after he missed the first several games with the same issue, and now, the team has gotten a rough update on his status moving forward.

"Hornets say Kon Knueppel has a left hamstring strain and will miss Friday's game against Boston. Knueppel made his debut last night but exited the game early in Brooklyn due to ongoing problems with his hamstring strain," reported ClutchPoints NBA insider Brett Siegel on X, formerly Twitter.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

It's been a tough start to the season for the Hornets, who have not exactly vindicated their decision to trade LaMelo Ball to the Minnesota Timberwolves over the summer. Knueppel nearly won the Rookie of the Year award last season, shattering the rookie record for three pointers made in a campaign, but his ongoing injury issues have spelled major issues for the Hornets so far this year, as the team is shooting below 30 percent from beyond the arc so far in 2026-27.

It remains to be seen how long this injury will keep Knueppel out of the lineup, but things certainly won't get any easier for the Hornets with Friday's game against the Celtics. Tipoff for that one is set for 7:00 pm ET in Charlotte.

articles.title: Isaiah Stewart Has 'No Regrets' About Trying to Fight LeBron James, Talks Viral Lakers-Pistons Video
articles.summary: Memphis Grizzlies center Isaiah Stewart said he doesn't regret his attempt to fight LeBron James in a 2021 game or his part in a February brawl involving a number of players from the Charlotte Hornets.
articles.body:
Memphis Grizzlies center Isaiah Stewart said he doesn't regret his attempt to fight LeBron James in a 2021 game or his part in a February brawl involving a number of players from the Charlotte Hornets.

"I don't have no regrets. I feel like there's lessons out of everything. Even going back to that first incident, Charlotte, I don't have no regrets," he told Andscape's Marc J. Spears (14:45 mark). "I don't care what people may perceive me as. I come to play basketball. I play the game a certain way. There have been times where I looked back and thought, 'Hey, I should have done that.' And I feel like teams have in their game plans, 'Hey, let's do something to trip him off, get him out of the game.' For me it's hard to respect you as a man if that's your game plan."

Stewart was suspended two games for his fracas with James and seven games for his part in February's fight. He has been suspended on five separate occasions during his career. In June, the Detroit Pistons traded him to the Memphis Grizzlies as part of a massive six-team trade.

He spent his first six seasons with Detroit. In seven games this season he's averaging 11.9 points and 3.4 rebounds as the Grizzlies' backup center.

articles.title: Kon Knueppel injury update: Hornets reveal forward has hamstring strain
articles.summary: After missing the first 8 games of the NBA season, Hornets star Kon Knueppel made his regular season debut Wednesday. It lasted fewer than 6 minutes.
articles.body:
The Charlotte Hornets seemingly got the exact news they did not want.

Not even six minutes into his regular season debut, Rookie of the Year runner up Kon Knueppel left a game Wednesday, Nov. 4 against the Brooklyn Nets , with what the team then called left leg soreness.

On the latest injury report that published Thursday, Nov. 5, however, the team confirmed that it was a left hamstring strain, which was the same injury that sidelined him for the season's first eight games. The Hornets also already declared Knueppel out for their game Friday, Nov. 6 against the Boston Celtics .

The injury took place midway through the first quarter of Charlotte's game against Brooklyn.

NBA's young stars to watch in 2026-27 season: 25 players under 25

Although there didn't appear to be a specific play in which Knueppel got hurt, he exited shortly after he dribbled the ball off his foot. During the play, Knueppel tried to dribble the ball behind his back but it caromed off his right leg, forcing him to take a small step as he tried to recover it. Immediately after the play, Knueppel limped but tried to stay in the game before quickly heading to the bench. He eventually went into the locker room and did not return.

After the game, Hornets coach Charles Lee told the local broadcast that he did not have an update on Knueppel and said he would be evaluated once the team returned to Charlotte later Wednesday.

Knueppel scored 3 points, all from free throws, missed his only shot attempt – a 3-pointer – and committed 2 turnovers in 5:51 on the floor against the Nets . He did not record any other statistic.

"Hopefully I can contribute in a capacity similar to last year, and with all the offseason work that I put in, even more," Knueppel told the Hornets broadcast in a pregame interview. "It might take me a little bit to get to that full capability, but tonight I'll be ready to go and help us get a win."

Last season, his first in the NBA after the Hornets selected him with the No. 4 overall pick in the 2025 NBA Draft, Knueppel recorded 18.5 points, 5.3 rebounds and 3.4 assists per game. He converted 3-pointers at a 42.5% clip and lost out to his college teammate at Duke, Cooper Flagg, for the Rookie of the Year honor.
